requirement: Build a tiny in-memory to-do library in Python with these separately testable features, each with pytest tests: (1) add a to-do item; (2) list all items; (3) mark an item complete; (4) delete an item; (5) rename an item; (6) set a due date on an item; (7) set a priority (high, medium or low) on an item; (8) filter items by status (open or complete); (9) search items by text; (10) export all items to JSON; (11) import items from JSON. Validate inputs and raise clear errors for unknown item ids.

spec.name: Tiny in-memory to-do library
spec.description: A Python module `todo.py` exposing a `TodoList` class (in-memory) plus exceptions `TodoError(Exception)`, `ValidationError(TodoError, ValueError)` and `ItemNotFoundError(TodoError, KeyError)`. Items are `TodoItem` dataclasses with fields id (int, auto-incremented from 1, never reused), text (str), complete (bool, default False), due_date (datetime.date or None), priority ('high'|'medium'|'low', default 'medium'). Each feature is a method on TodoList and has pytest tests in tests/test_<feature>.py. Standard library only.

acceptance_criteria.text: TodoList.add(text) returns a new TodoItem with a unique auto-incremented int id starting at 1, the stripped text, complete=False, due_date=None, priority='medium'. Ids are never reused after deletion.
add raises ValidationError if text is not a str or is empty/whitespace-only.
TodoList.list() returns all items as a list ordered by id ascending; an empty list when there are none. Mutating the returned list does not alter the TodoList.
TodoList.complete(item_id) sets complete=True on that item and returns it; calling it on an already complete item is allowed and leaves it complete.
TodoList.delete(item_id) removes the item so it no longer appears in list(); it returns the removed item.
TodoList.rename(item_id, new_text) updates the item's text (stripped) and returns the item; empty/whitespace-only or non-str new_text raises ValidationError and leaves the text unchanged.

TodoList.set_due_date(item_id, due) accepts a datetime.date or an ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' string (stored as datetime.date), or None to clear the due date; any other value or an invalid date string raises ValidationError. Returns the item.
TodoList.set_priority(item_id, priority) accepts exactly 'high', 'medium' or 'low' (case-sensitive) and returns the item; any other value raises ValidationError and leaves the priority unchanged.
TodoList.filter_by_status(status) returns items (ordered by id) that are open when status=='open' and complete when status=='complete'; any other status raises ValidationError.

TodoList.search(query) returns items (ordered by id) whose text contains the query as a case-insensitive substring; no matches gives an empty list; a non-str or empty/whitespace-only query raises ValidationError.
TodoList.export_json() returns a JSON string representing a list of all items, each object with keys id, text, complete, due_date (ISO string or null) and priority; an empty list exports as '[]'.

TodoList.import_json(json_str) replaces the list contents with the items parsed from JSON in the export format, preserving ids, and returns the number of items imported; subsequent add uses an id greater than the max imported id. A round trip export->import into a fresh TodoList yields equal items.

import_json raises ValidationError for invalid JSON, a top-level value that is not a list, items that are not objects, missing/wrongly-typed fields, invalid priority or due_date, empty text, or duplicate ids; on any such error the existing list is left unchanged.

Every method taking an item_id (complete, delete, rename, set_due_date, set_priority) raises ItemNotFoundError whose message includes the id when no such item exists, and ValidationError if item_id is not an int (bool excluded).

import datetime
import os
import sys

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..")))

from todo import (  # noqa: E402
    ItemNotFoundError,
    TodoError,
    TodoItem,
    TodoList,
    ValidationError,
)


def test_exception_hierarchy():
    assert issubclass(TodoError, Exception)
    assert issubclass(ValidationError, TodoError)
    assert issubclass(ValidationError, ValueError)
    assert issubclass(ItemNotFoundError, TodoError)
    assert issubclass(ItemNotFoundError, KeyError)


def test_add_returns_item_with_defaults():
    todo = TodoList()
    item = todo.add("  buy milk  ")
    assert isinstance(item, TodoItem)
    assert item.id == 1
    assert item.text == "buy milk"
    assert item.complete is False
    assert item.due_date is None
    assert item.priority == "medium"


def test_add_with_due_date_and_priority():
    todo = TodoList()
    d = datetime.date(2030, 1, 2)
    item = todo.add("x", due_date=d, priority="high")
    assert item.due_date == d
    assert item.priority == "high"


def test_second_add_gets_id_2():
    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("first")
    second = todo.add("second")
    assert second.id == 2


def test_ids_never_reused_after_list_mutation():
    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a")
    todo.add("b")
    listed = todo.list()
    listed.clear()
    assert todo.add("c").id == 3


@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", ["", "   ", "\t\n"])
def test_empty_or_whitespace_text_raises(bad):
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        TodoList().add(bad)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", [None, 5, 1.5, b"bytes", ["x"]])
def test_non_str_text_raises(bad):
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        TodoList().add(bad)


def test_invalid_priority_raises():
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        TodoList().add("x", priority="urgent")


def test_invalid_due_date_raises():
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        TodoList().add("x", due_date="2030-01-01")


def test_failed_add_does_not_consume_id():
    todo = TodoList()
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        todo.add("   ")
    assert todo.add("ok").id == 1

from todo import TodoItem, TodoList  # noqa: E402

    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a")
    todo.add("b")
    items = todo.list()
    items.pop()
    items.append(TodoItem(id=99, text="fake"))
    assert [i.text for i in todo.list()] == ["a", "b"]

    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a")
    todo.list()[0].text = "changed"
    todo.list()[0].complete = True
    stored = todo.list()[0]
    assert stored.text == "a"

# ===== todo.py =====
"""Tiny in-memory to-do library."""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import datetime
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional

PRIORITIES = ("high", "medium", "low")


class TodoError(Exception):
    """Base class for all to-do errors."""


class ValidationError(TodoError, ValueError):
    """Raised when input values are invalid."""


class ItemNotFoundError(TodoError, KeyError):
    """Raised when an item id does not exist."""

    def __str__(self) -> str:  # KeyError would otherwise repr-quote the message
        return Exception.__str__(self)


@dataclass
class TodoItem:
    id: int
    text: str
    complete: bool = False
    due_date: Optional[datetime.date] = None
    priority: str = "medium"


class TodoList:
    """In-memory collection of TodoItem objects."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._items: dict[int, TodoItem] = {}
        self._next_id: int = 1

    # ----- helpers -------------------------------------------------------
    def _get_item(self, item_id: object) -> TodoItem:
        """Return the stored item with ``item_id``.

        Raises ValidationError if the id is not a positive int, and
        ItemNotFoundError if no such item exists.
        """
        if isinstance(item_id, bool) or not isinstance(item_id, int):
            raise ValidationError(f"item id must be an int, got {type(item_id).__name__}")
        if item_id < 1:
            raise ValidationError(f"item id must be positive, got {item_id}")
        try:
            return self._items[item_id]
        except KeyError:
            raise ItemNotFoundError(f"no item with id {item_id}") from None

    # ----- public API ----------------------------------------------------
    def add(
        self,
        text: str,
        due_date: Optional[datetime.date] = None,
        priority: str = "medium",
    ) -> TodoItem:
        """Add a new item and return a copy of it."""
        if not isinstance(text, str):
            raise ValidationError(f"text must be a str, got {type(text).__name__}")
        stripped = text.strip()
        if not stripped:
            raise ValidationError("text must not be empty or whitespace-only")
        if due_date is not None and not isinstance(due_date, datetime.date):
            raise ValidationError("due_date must be a datetime.date or None")
        if priority not in PRIORITIES:
            raise ValidationError(f"priority must be one of {PRIORITIES}, got {priority!r}")

        item = TodoItem(
            id=self._next_id,
            text=stripped,
            complete=False,
            due_date=due_date,
            priority=priority,
        )
        self._items[item.id] = item
        self._next_id += 1
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def list(self) -> list[TodoItem]:
        """Return copies of all items, ordered by id."""
        return [dataclasses.replace(self._items[i]) for i in sorted(self._items)]

        self,
        text: str,

"""Tiny in-memory to-do library."""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import datetime
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional

# Module-level alias so annotations/helpers inside TodoList can still refer to
# the builtin ``list`` even though TodoList defines a method named ``list``.
_BuiltinList = list

PRIORITIES = ("high", "medium", "low")


class TodoError(Exception):
    """Base class for all to-do errors."""


class ValidationError(TodoError, ValueError):
    """Raised when input values are invalid."""


class ItemNotFoundError(TodoError, KeyError):
    """Raised when an item id does not exist."""

    def __str__(self) -> str:  # KeyError would otherwise repr-quote the message
        return Exception.__str__(self)


@dataclass
class TodoItem:
    id: int
    text: str
    complete: bool = False
    due_date: Optional[datetime.date] = None
    priority: str = "medium"


class TodoList:
    """In-memory collection of TodoItem objects."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._items: dict[int, TodoItem] = {}
        self._next_id: int = 1

    # ----- helpers -------------------------------------------------------
    def _get_item(self, item_id: object) -> TodoItem:
        """Return the stored item with ``item_id``.

        Raises ValidationError if the id is not a positive int, and
        ItemNotFoundError if no such item exists.
        """
        if isinstance(item_id, bool) or not isinstance(item_id, int):
            raise ValidationError(f"item id must be an int, got {type(item_id).__name__}")
        if item_id < 1:
            raise ValidationError(f"item id must be positive, got {item_id}")
        try:
            return self._items[item_id]
        except KeyError:
            raise ItemNotFoundError(f"no item with id {item_id}") from None

    # ----- public API ----------------------------------------------------
    def add(
        self,
        text: str,
        due_date: Optional[datetime.date] = None,
        priority: str = "medium",
    ) -> TodoItem:
        """Add a new item and return a copy of it.

        Only leading and trailing whitespace is stripped from ``text``;
        internal whitespace (including newlines) is preserved. ``due_date``
        must be a ``datetime.date`` (not a ``datetime.datetime``) or None.
        """
        if not isinstance(text, str):
            raise ValidationError(f"text must be a str, got {type(text).__name__}")
        stripped = text.strip()
        if not stripped:
            raise ValidationError("text must not be empty or whitespace-only")
        if due_date is not None and (
            not isinstance(due_date, datetime.date)
            or isinstance(due_date, datetime.datetime)
        ):
            raise ValidationError("due_date must be a datetime.date or None")
        if priority not in PRIORITIES:
            raise ValidationError(f"priority must be one of {PRIORITIES}, got {priority!r}")

        item = TodoItem(
            id=self._next_id,
            text=stripped,
            complete=False,
            due_date=due_date,
            priority=priority,
        )
        self._items[item.id] = item
        self._next_id += 1
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def list(self) -> _BuiltinList[TodoItem]:
        """Return copies of all items, ordered by id."""
        return [dataclasses.replace(self._items[i]) for i in sorted(self._items)]

    def complete(self, item_id: int) -> TodoItem:
        """Mark the item with ``item_id`` as complete and return a copy of it.

        Completing an already-complete item is allowed and is a no-op.
        Raises ValidationError for a non-int/bool id and ItemNotFoundError
        for an unknown id.
        """
        item = self._get_item(item_id)
        item.complete = True
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def delete(self, item_id: int) -> TodoItem:
        """Remove the item with ``item_id`` and return a copy of it.

        Ids are never reused: later add() calls continue from the highest
        id ever issued. Raises ValidationError for a non-int/bool id and
        ItemNotFoundError if the id is unknown (including already deleted).
        """
        item = self._get_item(item_id)
        del self._items[item.id]
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

# ===== todo.py =====
"""Tiny in-memory to-do library."""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import datetime
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional

# Module-level alias so annotations/helpers inside TodoList can still refer to
# the builtin ``list`` even though TodoList defines a method named ``list``.
_BuiltinList = list

PRIORITIES = ("high", "medium", "low")


class TodoError(Exception):
    """Base class for all to-do errors."""


class ValidationError(TodoError, ValueError):
    """Raised when input values are invalid."""


class ItemNotFoundError(TodoError, KeyError):
    """Raised when an item id does not exist."""

    def __str__(self) -> str:  # KeyError would otherwise repr-quote the message
        return Exception.__str__(self)


@dataclass
class TodoItem:
    id: int
    text: str
    complete: bool = False
    due_date: Optional[datetime.date] = None
    priority: str = "medium"


def _validate_text(text: object) -> str:
    """Return ``text`` stripped of leading/trailing whitespace, or raise."""
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        raise ValidationError(f"text must be a str, got {type(text).__name__}")
    stripped = text.strip()
    if not stripped:
        raise ValidationError("text must not be empty or whitespace-only")
    return stripped


def _validate_due_date(due: object) -> Optional[datetime.date]:
    """Normalise a due date: None, a datetime.date, or an ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' str.

    datetime.datetime values are rejected. Anything else raises ValidationError.
    """
    if due is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(due, datetime.datetime):
        raise ValidationError("due_date must be a datetime.date, not datetime.datetime")
    if isinstance(due, datetime.date):
        return due
    if isinstance(due, str):
        try:
            return datetime.date.fromisoformat(due)
        except ValueError:
            raise ValidationError(f"due_date string must be YYYY-MM-DD, got {due!r}") from None
    raise ValidationError(
        f"due_date must be a date, an ISO date string or None, got {type(due).__name__}"
    )


def _validate_priority(priority: object) -> str:
    """Return ``priority`` if it is one of PRIORITIES, otherwise raise."""
    if not isinstance(priority, str) or priority not in PRIORITIES:
        raise ValidationError(f"priority must be one of {PRIORITIES}, got {priority!r}")
    return priority


class TodoList:
    """In-memory collection of TodoItem objects."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._items: dict[int, TodoItem] = {}
        self._next_id: int = 1

    # ----- helpers -------------------------------------------------------
    def _get_item(self, item_id: object) -> TodoItem:
        """Return the stored item with ``item_id``.

        Raises ValidationError if the id is not a positive int, and
        ItemNotFoundError if no such item exists.
        """
        if isinstance(item_id, bool) or not isinstance(item_id, int):
            raise ValidationError(f"item id must be an int, got {type(item_id).__name__}")
        if item_id < 1:
            raise ValidationError(f"item id must be positive, got {item_id}")
        try:
            return self._items[item_id]
        except KeyError:
            raise ItemNotFoundError(f"no item with id {item_id}") from None

    # ----- public API ----------------------------------------------------
    def add(
        self,
        text: str,
        due_date: Optional[datetime.date] = None,
        priority: str = "medium",
    ) -> TodoItem:
        """Add a new item and return a copy of it.

        Only leading and trailing whitespace is stripped from ``text``;
        internal whitespace (including newlines) is preserved. ``due_date``
        must be a ``datetime.date`` (not a ``datetime.datetime``) or None.
        """
        stripped = _validate_text(text)
        due = _validate_due_date(due_date) if due_date is not None else None
        if due_date is not None and not isinstance(due_date, datetime.date):
            # add() historically only accepts date objects, not ISO strings.
            raise ValidationError("due_date must be a datetime.date or None")
        _validate_priority(priority)

        item = TodoItem(
            id=self._next_id,
            text=stripped,
            complete=False,
            due_date=due,
            priority=priority,
        )
        self._items[item.id] = item
        self._next_id += 1
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def list(self) -> _BuiltinList[TodoItem]:
        """Return copies of all items, ordered by id."""
        return [dataclasses.replace(self._items[i]) for i in sorted(self._items)]

    def complete(self, item_id: int) -> TodoItem:
        """Mark the item with ``item_id`` as complete and return a copy of it.

        Completing an already-complete item is allowed and is a no-op.
        Raises ValidationError for a non-int/bool id and ItemNotFoundError
        for an unknown id.
        """
        item = self._get_item(item_id)
        item.complete = True
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def delete(self, item_id: int) -> TodoItem:
        """Remove the item with ``item_id`` and return a copy of it.

        Ids are never reused: later add() calls continue from the highest
        id ever issued. Raises ValidationError for a non-int/bool id and
        ItemNotFoundError if the id is unknown (including already deleted).
        """
        item = self._get_item(item_id)
        del self._items[item.id]
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def rename(self, item_id: int, new_text: str) -> TodoItem:
        """Replace the text of an item and return a copy of it.

        ``new_text`` is stripped like add(). On ValidationError the stored text
        is left unchanged. Raises ItemNotFoundError for an unknown id.
        """
        item = self._get_item(item_id)
        item.text = _validate_text(new_text)
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def set_due_date(self, item_id: int, due: object) -> TodoItem:
        """Set (or clear, with None) the due date of an item and return a copy.

        Accepts a datetime.date, an ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' string, or None.
        datetime.datetime, malformed strings and other types raise
        ValidationError and leave the stored date unchanged.
        """
        item = self._get_item(item_id)
        item.due_date = _validate_due_date(due)
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def set_priority(self, item_id: int, priority: str) -> TodoItem:
        """Set the priority of an item ('high', 'medium' or 'low') and return a copy.

        Any other value (including wrong case or None) raises ValidationError
        and leaves the stored priority unchanged.
        """
        item = self._get_item(item_id)
        item.priority = _validate_priority(priority)
        return dataclasses.replace(item)
result.explanation: Added three methods to TodoList in todo.py, built on the existing _get_item helper. rename(item_id, new_text) strips the text and rejects empty, whitespace-only and non-str values with ValidationError, leaving the stored text unchanged. set_due_date(item_id, due) accepts a datetime.date, an ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' string, or None (which clears the date); it rejects datetime.datetime, malformed strings such as '2025-13-01' and 'abc', and non-str/non-date types such as 5, with ValidationError and no change to the stored date. set_priority(item_id, priority) accepts only 'high', 'medium' and 'low' and rejects 'urgent', 'HIGH' and None with ValidationError, leaving the priority unchanged. All three raise ItemNotFoundError (a KeyError, with the id in the message) for unknown or deleted ids, raise ValidationError for bool, non-int and non-positive ids, and return copies. import datetime
import os
import sys

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..")))

from todo import ItemNotFoundError, TodoItem, TodoList, ValidationError  # noqa: E402


def _list_with_one():
    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a")
    return todo


def test_set_due_date_stores_date_object():
    todo = _list_with_one()
    result = todo.set_due_date(1, datetime.date(2025, 3, 4))
    assert isinstance(result, TodoItem)
    assert result.due_date == datetime.date(2025, 3, 4)
    assert todo.list()[0].due_date == datetime.date(2025, 3, 4)


def test_set_due_date_accepts_iso_string():
    todo = _list_with_one()
    result = todo.set_due_date(1, "2025-01-31")
    assert result.due_date == datetime.date(2025, 1, 31)
    assert isinstance(result.due_date, datetime.date)
    assert todo.list()[0].due_date == datetime.date(2025, 1, 31)


def test_set_due_date_none_clears_date():
    todo = _list_with_one()
    todo.set_due_date(1, "2025-01-31")
    result = todo.set_due_date(1, None)
    assert result.due_date is None
    assert todo.list()[0].due_date is None


def test_set_due_date_keeps_other_fields():
    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a", priority="low")
    todo.complete(1)
    result = todo.set_due_date(1, "2030-06-15")
    assert result.text == "a"
    assert result.complete is True
    assert result.priority == "low"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "bad",
    [
        "2025-13-01",
        "2025-02-30",
        "abc",
        5,
        "",
        "2025-01-31T10:00",
        "20250131",
        "2025-W05-1",
        " 2025-01-31 ",
        "2025-1-5",
        "2025-01-31\n",
        b"2025-01-31",
    ],
)

    todo = _list_with_one()

    assert todo.list()[0].due_date == datetime.date(2025, 1, 1)

def test_set_due_date_bad_id_raises_validation_error(bad):

    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):

"""Tiny in-memory to-do library."""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import datetime
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional

# Module-level alias so annotations/helpers inside TodoList can still refer to
# the builtin ``list`` even though TodoList defines a method named ``list``.
_BuiltinList = list

PRIORITIES = ("high", "medium", "low")

_ISO_DATE_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}")


class TodoError(Exception):
    """Base class for all to-do errors."""


class ValidationError(TodoError, ValueError):
    """Raised when input values are invalid."""


class ItemNotFoundError(TodoError, KeyError):
    """Raised when an item id does not exist."""

    def __str__(self) -> str:  # KeyError would otherwise repr-quote the message
        return Exception.__str__(self)


@dataclass
class TodoItem:
    id: int
    text: str
    complete: bool = False
    due_date: Optional[datetime.date] = None
    priority: str = "medium"


def _validate_text(text: object) -> str:
    """Return ``text`` stripped of leading/trailing whitespace, or raise."""
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        raise ValidationError(f"text must be a str, got {type(text).__name__}")
    stripped = text.strip()
    if not stripped:
        raise ValidationError("text must not be empty or whitespace-only")
    return stripped


def _validate_due_date(due: object) -> Optional[datetime.date]:
    """Normalise a due date: None, a datetime.date, or a strict 'YYYY-MM-DD' str.

    datetime.datetime values are rejected. Strings must match YYYY-MM-DD exactly
    (no surrounding whitespace, no basic/week formats). Anything else raises
    ValidationError.
    """
    if due is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(due, datetime.datetime):
        raise ValidationError("due_date must be a datetime.date, not datetime.datetime")
    if isinstance(due, datetime.date):
        return due
    if isinstance(due, str):
        if not _ISO_DATE_RE.fullmatch(due):
            raise ValidationError(f"due_date string must be YYYY-MM-DD, got {due!r}")
        try:
            return datetime.date.fromisoformat(due)
        except ValueError:
            raise ValidationError(f"due_date string must be a valid date, got {due!r}") from None
    raise ValidationError(

# ===== tests/test_filter.py =====
import os
import sys

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..")))

from todo import TodoItem, TodoList, ValidationError  # noqa: E402


def _populated():
    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a")        # 1 open
    todo.add("b")        # 2 complete
    todo.add("c")        # 3 open
    todo.add("d")        # 4 complete
    todo.complete(2)
    todo.complete(4)
    return todo


def test_open_returns_only_incomplete_items_ordered_by_id():
    result = _populated().filter_by_status("open")
    assert all(isinstance(i, TodoItem) for i in result)
    assert [i.id for i in result] == [1, 3]
    assert all(i.complete is False for i in result)


def test_complete_returns_only_completed_items_ordered_by_id():
    result = _populated().filter_by_status("complete")
    assert [i.id for i in result] == [2, 4]
    assert all(i.complete is True for i in result)


def test_empty_list_filters_return_empty():
    todo = TodoList()
    assert todo.filter_by_status("open") == []
    assert todo.filter_by_status("complete") == []


def test_no_matches_returns_empty_list():
    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a")
    assert todo.filter_by_status("complete") == []


def test_ordering_holds_after_completing_out_of_order():
    todo = TodoList()
    for t in "abcd":
        todo.add(t)
    todo.complete(4)
    todo.complete(1)
    assert [i.id for i in todo.filter_by_status("complete")] == [1, 4]
    assert [i.id for i in todo.filter_by_status("open")] == [2, 3]


def test_filter_returns_copies():
    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a")
    result = todo.filter_by_status("open")
    result[0].text = "changed"
    result.clear()
    assert todo.list()[0].text == "a"
    assert len(todo.filter_by_status("open")) == 1


@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", ["", "OPEN", "Complete", "done", " open", None, 1, True, ["open"]])
def test_invalid_status_raises_validation_error(bad):
    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a")
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        todo.filter_by_status(bad)

import os

import pytest

# ===== todo.py =====
"""Tiny in-memory to-do library."""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import datetime
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional

# Module-level alias so annotations/helpers inside TodoList can still refer to
# the builtin ``list`` even though TodoList defines a method named ``list``.
_BuiltinList = list

PRIORITIES = ("high", "medium", "low")
STATUSES = ("open", "complete")

_ISO_DATE_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}")


class TodoError(Exception):
    """Base class for all to-do errors."""


class ValidationError(TodoError, ValueError):
    """Raised when input values are invalid."""


class ItemNotFoundError(TodoError, KeyError):
    """Raised when an item id does not exist."""

    def __str__(self) -> str:  # KeyError would otherwise repr-quote the message
        return Exception.__str__(self)


@dataclass
class TodoItem:
    id: int
    text: str
    complete: bool = False
    due_date: Optional[datetime.date] = None
    priority: str = "medium"


def _validate_text(text: object) -> str:
    """Return ``text`` stripped of leading/trailing whitespace, or raise."""
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        raise ValidationError(f"text must be a str, got {type(text).__name__}")
    stripped = text.strip()
    if not stripped:
        raise ValidationError("text must not be empty or whitespace-only")
    return stripped


def _validate_due_date(due: object) -> Optional[datetime.date]:
    """Normalise a due date: None, a datetime.date, or a strict 'YYYY-MM-DD' str.

    datetime.datetime values are rejected. Strings must match YYYY-MM-DD exactly
    (no surrounding whitespace, no basic/week formats). Anything else raises
    ValidationError.
    """
    if due is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(due, datetime.datetime):
        raise ValidationError("due_date must be a datetime.date, not datetime.datetime")
    if isinstance(due, datetime.date):
        return due
    if isinstance(due, str):
        if not _ISO_DATE_RE.fullmatch(due):
            raise ValidationError(f"due_date string must be YYYY-MM-DD, got {due!r}")
        try:
            return datetime.date.fromisoformat(due)
        except ValueError:
            raise ValidationError(f"due_date string must be a valid date, got {due!r}") from None
    raise ValidationError(
        f"due_date must be a date, an ISO date string or None, got {type(due).__name__}"
    )


def _validate_priority(priority: object) -> str:
    """Return ``priority`` as a plain str if it is one of PRIORITIES, otherwise raise.

    Only exact ``str`` instances are accepted, so str subclasses are rejected
    and never stored.
    """
    if type(priority) is not str or priority not in PRIORITIES:
        raise ValidationError(f"priority must be one of {PRIORITIES}, got {priority!r}")
    return priority


def _validate_status(status: object) -> str:
    """Return ``status`` if it is exactly 'open' or 'complete', otherwise raise."""
    if type(status) is not str or status not in STATUSES:
        raise ValidationError(f"status must be one of {STATUSES}, got {status!r}")
    return status


def _validate_query(query: object) -> str:
    """Return ``query`` stripped of surrounding whitespace, or raise."""
    if not isinstance(query, str):
        raise ValidationError(f"query must be a str, got {type(query).__name__}")
    stripped = query.strip()
    if not stripped:
        raise ValidationError("query must not be empty or whitespace-only")
    return stripped


class TodoList:
    """In-memory collection of TodoItem objects.

    Precedence for all item-targeting methods: the id is validated and looked
    up first (ValidationError for a bad id type/value, ItemNotFoundError for an
    unknown id), then the new value is validated. Values are validated before
    the stored item is touched, so a failed call never changes state.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._items: dict[int, TodoItem] = {}
        self._next_id: int = 1

    # ----- helpers -------------------------------------------------------
    def _get_item(self, item_id: object) -> TodoItem:
        """Return the stored item with ``item_id``.

        Raises ValidationError if the id is not a positive int, and
        ItemNotFoundError if no such item exists.
        """
        if isinstance(item_id, bool) or not isinstance(item_id, int):
            raise ValidationError(f"item id must be an int, got {type(item_id).__name__}")
        if item_id < 1:
            raise ValidationError(f"item id must be positive, got {item_id}")
        try:
            return self._items[item_id]
        except KeyError:
            raise ItemNotFoundError(f"no item with id {item_id}") from None

    # ----- public API ----------------------------------------------------
    def add(
        self,
        text: str,
        due_date: Optional[datetime.date] = None,
        priority: str = "medium",
    ) -> TodoItem:
        """Add a new item and return a copy of it.

        Only leading and trailing whitespace is stripped from ``text``;
        internal whitespace (including newlines) is preserved. ``due_date``

            text=stripped,
            complete=False,
            due_date=due,
            priority=checked_priority,

        self._next_id += 1
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

import os
import sys

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..")))

from todo import TodoItem, TodoList, ValidationError  # noqa: E402


def _populated():
    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a")        # 1 open
    todo.add("b")        # 2 complete
    todo.add("c")        # 3 open
    todo.add("d")        # 4 complete
    todo.complete(2)
    todo.complete(4)
    return todo


def test_open_returns_only_incomplete_items_ordered_by_id():
    result = _populated().filter_by_status("open")
    assert all(isinstance(i, TodoItem) for i in result)
    assert [i.id for i in result] == [1, 3]
    assert all(i.complete is False for i in result)


def test_complete_returns_only_completed_items_ordered_by_id():
    result = _populated().filter_by_status("complete")
    assert [i.id for i in result] == [2, 4]
    assert all(i.complete is True for i in result)


def test_empty_list_filters_return_empty():
    todo = TodoList()
    assert todo.filter_by_status("open") == []
    assert todo.filter_by_status("complete") == []


def test_no_matches_returns_empty_list():
    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a")
    assert todo.filter_by_status("complete") == []


def test_ordering_holds_after_completing_out_of_order():
    todo = TodoList()
    for t in "abcd":
        todo.add(t)
    todo.complete(4)
    todo.complete(1)
    assert [i.id for i in todo.filter_by_status("complete")] == [1, 4]
    assert [i.id for i in todo.filter_by_status("open")] == [2, 3]


def test_filter_returns_copies():
    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a")
    result = todo.filter_by_status("open")
    result[0].text = "changed"
    result.clear()
    assert todo.list()[0].text == "a"
    assert len(todo.filter_by_status("open")) == 1


@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", ["", "OPEN", "Complete", "done", " open", None, 1, True, ["open"]])
def test_invalid_status_raises_validation_error(bad):
    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a")
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        todo.filter_by_status(bad)

"""Tiny in-memory to-do library."""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import datetime
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional

# Module-level alias so annotations/helpers inside TodoList can still refer to
# the builtin ``list`` even though TodoList defines a method named ``list``.
_BuiltinList = list

PRIORITIES = ("high", "medium", "low")
STATUSES = ("open", "complete")

_ISO_DATE_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}")


class TodoError(Exception):
    """Base class for all to-do errors."""


class ValidationError(TodoError, ValueError):
    """Raised when input values are invalid."""


class ItemNotFoundError(TodoError, KeyError):
    """Raised when an item id does not exist."""

    def __str__(self) -> str:  # KeyError would otherwise repr-quote the message
        return Exception.__str__(self)


@dataclass
class TodoItem:
    id: int
    text: str
    complete: bool = False
    due_date: Optional[datetime.date] = None
    priority: str = "medium"


def _validate_text(text: object) -> str:
    """Return ``text`` stripped of leading/trailing whitespace, or raise."""
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        raise ValidationError(f"text must be a str, got {type(text).__name__}")
    stripped = text.strip()
    if not stripped:
        raise ValidationError("text must not be empty or whitespace-only")
    return stripped


def _validate_due_date(due: object) -> Optional[datetime.date]:
    """Normalise a due date: None, a datetime.date, or a strict 'YYYY-MM-DD' str.

    datetime.datetime values are rejected. Strings must match YYYY-MM-DD exactly
    (no surrounding whitespace, no basic/week formats). Anything else raises
    ValidationError.
    """
    if due is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(due, datetime.datetime):
        raise ValidationError("due_date must be a datetime.date, not datetime.datetime")
    if isinstance(due, datetime.date):
        return due
    if isinstance(due, str):
        if not _ISO_DATE_RE.fullmatch(due):
            raise ValidationError(f"due_date string must be YYYY-MM-DD, got {due!r}")
        try:
            return datetime.date.fromisoformat(due)
        except ValueError:
            raise ValidationError(f"due_date string must be a valid date, got {due!r}") from None
    raise ValidationError(
        f"due_date must be a date, an ISO date string or None, got {type(due).__name__}"
    )


def _validate_priority(priority: object) -> str:
    """Return ``priority`` as a plain str if it is one of PRIORITIES, otherwise raise.

    Only exact ``str`` instances are accepted, so str subclasses are rejected
    and never stored.
    """
    if type(priority) is not str or priority not in PRIORITIES:
        raise ValidationError(f"priority must be one of {PRIORITIES}, got {priority!r}")
    return priority


def _validate_status(status: object) -> str:
    """Return ``status`` if it is exactly 'open' or 'complete', otherwise raise."""
    if type(status) is not str or status not in STATUSES:
        raise ValidationError(f"status must be one of {STATUSES}, got {status!r}")
    return status


def _validate_query(query: object) -> str:
    """Return ``query`` stripped of surrounding whitespace, or raise."""
    if not isinstance(query, str):
        raise ValidationError(f"query must be a str, got {type(query).__name__}")
    stripped = query.strip()
    if not stripped:
        raise ValidationError("query must not be empty or whitespace-only")
    return stripped


class TodoList:
    """In-memory collection of TodoItem objects.

    Precedence for all item-targeting methods: the id is validated and looked
    up first (ValidationError for a bad id type/value, ItemNotFoundError for an
    unknown id), then the new value is validated. Values are validated before
    the stored item is touched, so a failed call never changes state.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._items: dict[int, TodoItem] = {}
        self._next_id: int = 1

    # ----- helpers -------------------------------------------------------
    def _get_item(self, item_id: object) -> TodoItem:
        """Return the stored item with ``item_id``.

        Raises ValidationError if the id is not a positive int, and
        ItemNotFoundError if no such item exists.
        """
        if isinstance(item_id, bool) or not isinstance(item_id, int):
            raise ValidationError(f"item id must be an int, got {type(item_id).__name__}")
        if item_id < 1:
            raise ValidationError(f"item id must be positive, got {item_id}")
        try:
            return self._items[item_id]
        except KeyError:
            raise ItemNotFoundError(f"no item with id {item_id}") from None

    # ----- public API ----------------------------------------------------
    def add(
        self,
        text: str,
        due_date: Optional[datetime.date] = None,
        priority: str = "medium",
    ) -> TodoItem:
        """Add a new item and return a copy of it.

        Only leading and trailing whitespace is stripped from ``text``;
        internal whitespace (including newlines) is preserved. ``due_date``
        must be a ``datetime.date`` or None (ISO strings are not accepted by
        add(); use set_due_date() for those).
        """
        stripped = _validate_text(text)
        if due_date is not None and not isinstance(due_date, datetime.date):
            raise ValidationError("due_date must be a datetime.date or None")
        due = _validate_due_date(due_date)
        checked_priority = _validate_priority(priority)

        item = TodoItem(
            id=self._next_id,
            text=stripped,
            complete=False,
            due_date=due,
            priority=checked_priority,
        )
        self._items[item.id] = item
        self._next_id += 1
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def list(self) -> _BuiltinList[TodoItem]:
        """Return copies of all items, ordered by id."""
        return [dataclasses.replace(self._items[i]) for i in sorted(self._items)]

    def complete(self, item_id: int) -> TodoItem:
        """Mark the item with ``item_id`` as complete and return a copy of it.

        Completing an already-complete item is allowed and is a no-op.
        Raises ValidationError for a non-int/bool id and ItemNotFoundError
        for an unknown id.
        """
        item = self._get_item(item_id)
        item.complete = True
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def delete(self, item_id: int) -> TodoItem:
        """Remove the item with ``item_id`` and return a copy of it.

        Ids are never reused: later add() calls continue from the highest
        id ever issued. Raises ValidationError for a non-int/bool id and
        ItemNotFoundError if the id is unknown (including already deleted).
        """
        item = self._get_item(item_id)
        del self._items[item.id]
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def rename(self, item_id: int, new_text: str) -> TodoItem:
        """Replace the text of an item and return a copy of it.

        ``new_text`` is stripped like add(). The id is checked before the text.
        On ValidationError the stored text is left unchanged. Raises
        ItemNotFoundError for an unknown id.
        """
        item = self._get_item(item_id)
        checked_text = _validate_text(new_text)
        item.text = checked_text
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def set_due_date(self, item_id: int, due: object) -> TodoItem:
        """Set (or clear, with None) the due date of an item and return a copy.

        Accepts a datetime.date, a strict 'YYYY-MM-DD' string, or None. The id
        is checked before the date. datetime.datetime, malformed or padded
        strings and other types raise ValidationError and leave the stored
        date unchanged.
        """
        item = self._get_item(item_id)
        checked_due = _validate_due_date(due)
        item.due_date = checked_due
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def set_priority(self, item_id: int, priority: str) -> TodoItem:
        """Set the priority of an item ('high', 'medium' or 'low') and return a copy.

        The id is checked before the priority. Any other value (including
        wrong case, None, or str subclasses) raises ValidationError and leaves
        the stored priority unchanged.
        """
        item = self._get_item(item_id)
        checked_priority = _validate_priority(priority)
        item.priority = checked_priority
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def filter_by_status(self, status: str) -> _BuiltinList[TodoItem]:
        """Return copies of items matching ``status``, ordered by id.

        ``status`` must be exactly 'open' (incomplete items) or 'complete'
        (completed items). Anything else raises ValidationError.
        """
        checked = _validate_status(status)
        want_complete = checked == "complete"
        return [
            dataclasses.replace(self._items[i])
            for i in sorted(self._items)
            if self._items[i].complete is want_complete
        ]

    def search(self, query: str) -> _BuiltinList[TodoItem]:
        """Return copies of items whose text contains ``query``, ordered by id.

        Matching is a case-insensitive substring match (casefold). The query
        is stripped of surrounding whitespace first; empty, whitespace-only or
        non-str queries raise ValidationError. No match returns [].
        """
        needle = _validate_query(query).casefold()
        return [
            dataclasses.replace(self._items[i])
            for i in sorted(self._items)
            if needle in self._items[i].text.casefold()
        ]

import os
import sys

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..")))

from todo import TodoItem, TodoList, ValidationError  # noqa: E402


class _OpenStr(str):
    """A str subclass whose value equals 'open'."""


def _populated():
    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a")        # 1 open
    todo.add("b")        # 2 complete
    todo.add("c")        # 3 open
    todo.add("d")        # 4 complete
    todo.complete(2)
    todo.complete(4)
    return todo


def test_open_returns_only_incomplete_items_ordered_by_id():
    result = _populated().filter_by_status("open")
    assert all(isinstance(i, TodoItem) for i in result)
    assert [i.id for i in result] == [1, 3]
    assert all(i.complete is False for i in result)


def test_complete_returns_only_completed_items_ordered_by_id():
    result = _populated().filter_by_status("complete")
    assert [i.id for i in result] == [2, 4]
    assert all(i.complete is True for i in result)


def test_empty_list_filters_return_empty():
    todo = TodoList()
    assert todo.filter_by_status("open") == []
    assert todo.filter_by_status("complete") == []


def test_no_matches_returns_empty_list():
    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a")
    assert todo.filter_by_status("complete") == []


def test_ordering_holds_after_completing_out_of_order():
    todo = TodoList()
    for t in "abcd":
        todo.add(t)
    todo.complete(4)
    todo.complete(1)
    assert [i.id for i in todo.filter_by_status("complete")] == [1, 4]
    assert [i.id for i in todo.filter_by_status("open")] == [2, 3]


def test_filter_after_delete_skips_gaps_and_stays_ordered():
    todo = TodoList()
    for t in "abcd":
        todo.add(t)      # ids 1..4
    todo.delete(1)
    todo.delete(3)
    todo.complete(4)
    assert [i.id for i in todo.filter_by_status("open")] == [2]
    assert [i.id for i in todo.filter_by_status("complete")] == [4]
    todo.add("e")        # id 5, never reuses 1 or 3
    assert [i.id for i in todo.filter_by_status("open")] == [2, 5]


def test_filter_returns_copies():
    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a")
    result = todo.filter_by_status("open")
    result[0].text = "changed"
    result.clear()
    assert todo.list()[0].text == "a"
    assert len(todo.filter_by_status("open")) == 1


def test_later_complete_does_not_change_earlier_filter_result():
    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a")
    earlier = todo.filter_by_status("open")
    todo.complete(1)
    assert earlier[0].complete is False
    assert todo.filter_by_status("open") == []

    "bad",

)

    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a")
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        todo.filter_by_status(bad)

"""Tiny in-memory to-do library."""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import datetime
import re
import unicodedata
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional

# Module-level alias so annotations/helpers inside TodoList can still refer to
# the builtin ``list`` even though TodoList defines a method named ``list``.
_BuiltinList = list

PRIORITIES = ("high", "medium", "low")
STATUSES = ("open", "complete")

_ISO_DATE_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}")


class TodoError(Exception):
    """Base class for all to-do errors."""


class ValidationError(TodoError, ValueError):
    """Raised when input values are invalid."""


class ItemNotFoundError(TodoError, KeyError):
    """Raised when an item id does not exist."""

    def __str__(self) -> str:  # KeyError would otherwise repr-quote the message
        return Exception.__str__(self)


@dataclass
class TodoItem:
    id: int
    text: str
    complete: bool = False
    due_date: Optional[datetime.date] = None
    priority: str = "medium"


def _validate_text(text: object) -> str:
    """Return ``text`` stripped of leading/trailing whitespace, or raise.

    Only leading/trailing whitespace is removed; internal whitespace and
    newlines are kept as given.
    """
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        raise ValidationError(f"text must be a str, got {type(text).__name__}")
    stripped = text.strip()
    if not stripped:
        raise ValidationError("text must not be empty or whitespace-only")
    return stripped


def _validate_due_date(due: object) -> Optional[datetime.date]:
    """Normalise a due date: None, a datetime.date, or a strict 'YYYY-MM-DD' str.

    datetime.datetime values are rejected. Strings must match YYYY-MM-DD exactly
    (no surrounding whitespace, no basic/week formats). Anything else raises
    ValidationError.
    """
    if due is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(due, datetime.datetime):
        raise ValidationError("due_date must be a datetime.date, not datetime.datetime")
    if isinstance(due, datetime.date):
        return due
    if isinstance(due, str):
        if not _ISO_DATE_RE.fullmatch(due):
            raise ValidationError(f"due_date string must be YYYY-MM-DD, got {due!r}")
        try:
            return datetime.date.fromisoformat(due)
        except ValueError:
            raise ValidationError(f"due_date string must be a valid date, got {due!r}") from None
    raise ValidationError(
        f"due_date must be a date, an ISO date string or None, got {type(due).__name__}"
    )


def _validate_priority(priority: object) -> str:
    """Return ``priority`` as a plain str if it is one of PRIORITIES, otherwise raise.

    Only exact ``str`` instances are accepted, so str subclasses are rejected
    and never stored.
    """
    if type(priority) is not str or priority not in PRIORITIES:
        raise ValidationError(f"priority must be one of {PRIORITIES}, got {priority!r}")
    return priority


def _validate_status(status: object) -> str:
    """Return ``status`` if it is exactly 'open' or 'complete', otherwise raise.

    Only exact ``str`` instances are accepted; str subclasses are rejected.
    """
    if type(status) is not str or status not in STATUSES:
        raise ValidationError(f"status must be one of {STATUSES}, got {status!r}")
    return status


def _validate_query(query: object) -> str:
    """Return ``query`` stripped of surrounding whitespace, or raise.

    Surrounding whitespace is any Unicode whitespace that ``str.strip`` removes
    (including U+00A0 and U+3000). Internal whitespace is kept as given, so
    'buy  milk' (two spaces) does not match 'buy milk'.
    """
    if not isinstance(query, str):
        raise ValidationError(f"query must be a str, got {type(query).__name__}")
    stripped = query.strip()
    if not stripped:
        raise ValidationError("query must not be empty or whitespace-only")
    return stripped


def _fold(s: str) -> str:
    """Normalise text for case-insensitive matching: NFKC then casefold."""
    return unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", s).casefold()


class TodoList:
    """In-memory collection of TodoItem objects.

    Precedence for all item-targeting methods: the id is validated and looked
    up first (ValidationError for a bad id type/value, ItemNotFoundError for an
    unknown id), then the new value is validated. Values are validated before
    the stored item is touched, so a failed call never changes state.

    Returned items are shallow copies: mutating them does not change the store.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._items: dict[int, TodoItem] = {}
        self._next_id: int = 1

    # ----- helpers -------------------------------------------------------
    def _get_item(self, item_id: object) -> TodoItem:
        """Return the stored item with ``item_id``.

        Raises ValidationError if the id is not a positive int, and
        ItemNotFoundError if no such item exists.
        """
        if isinstance(item_id, bool) or not isinstance(item_id, int):
            raise ValidationError(f"item id must be an int, got {type(item_id).__name__}")
        if item_id < 1:
            raise ValidationError(f"item id must be positive, got {item_id}")
        try:
            return self._items[item_id]
        except KeyError:
            raise ItemNotFoundError(f"no item with id {item_id}") from None

    # ----- public API ----------------------------------------------------
    def add(
        self,
        text: str,
        due_date: Optional[datetime.date] = None,
        priority: str = "medium",
    ) -> TodoItem:
        """Add a new item and return a copy of it.

        Only leading and trailing whitespace is stripped from ``text``;
        internal whitespace (including newlines) is preserved. ``due_date``
        must be a ``datetime.date`` or None (ISO strings are not accepted by
        add(); use set_due_date() for those).
        """
        stripped = _validate_text(text)
        if due_date is not None and not isinstance(due_date, datetime.date):
            raise ValidationError("due_date must be a datetime.date or None")
        due = _validate_due_date(due_date)
        checked_priority = _validate_priority(priority)

        item = TodoItem(
            id=self._next_id,
            text=stripped,
            complete=False,
            due_date=due,
            priority=checked_priority,
        )
        self._items[item.id] = item
        self._next_id += 1
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def list(self) -> _BuiltinList[TodoItem]:
        """Return copies of all items, ordered by id."""
        return [dataclasses.replace(self._items[i]) for i in sorted(self._items)]

    def complete(self, item_id: int) -> TodoItem:
        """Mark the item with ``item_id`` as complete and return a copy of it.

        Completing an already-complete item is allowed and is a no-op.
        Raises ValidationError for a non-int/bool id and ItemNotFoundError
        for an unknown id.
        """
        item = self._get_item(item_id)
        item.complete = True
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def delete(self, item_id: int) -> TodoItem:
        """Remove the item with ``item_id`` and return a copy of it.

        Ids are never reused: later add() calls continue from the highest
        id ever issued. Raises ValidationError for a non-int/bool id and
        ItemNotFoundError if the id is unknown (including already deleted).
        """
        item = self._get_item(item_id)
        del self._items[item.id]
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def rename(self, item_id: int, new_text: str) -> TodoItem:
        """Replace the text of an item and return a copy of it.

        ``new_text`` is stripped like add(). The id is checked before the text.
        On ValidationError the stored text is left unchanged. Raises
        ItemNotFoundError for an unknown id.
        """
        item = self._get_item(item_id)
        checked_text = _validate_text(new_text)
        item.text = checked_text
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def set_due_date(self, item_id: int, due: object) -> TodoItem:
        """Set (or clear, with None) the due date of an item and return a copy.

        Accepts a datetime.date, a strict 'YYYY-MM-DD' string, or None. The id
        is checked before the date. datetime.datetime, malformed or padded
        strings and other types raise ValidationError and leave the stored
        date unchanged.
        """
        item = self._get_item(item_id)
        checked_due = _validate_due_date(due)
        item.due_date = checked_due
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def set_priority(self, item_id: int, priority: str) -> TodoItem:
        """Set the priority of an item ('high', 'medium' or 'low') and return a copy.

        The id is checked before the priority. Any other value (including
        wrong case, None, or str subclasses) raises ValidationError and leaves
        the stored priority unchanged.
        """
        item = self._get_item(item_id)
        checked_priority = _validate_priority(priority)
        item.priority = checked_priority
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def filter_by_status(self, status: str) -> _BuiltinList[TodoItem]:
        """Return copies of items matching ``status``, ordered by id.

        ``status`` must be exactly 'open' (incomplete items) or 'complete'
        (completed items). Anything else, including str subclasses, raises
        ValidationError.
        """
        checked = _validate_status(status)
        want_complete = checked == "complete"
        return [
            dataclasses.replace(self._items[i])
            for i in sorted(self._items)
            if self._items[i].complete is want_complete
        ]

    def search(self, query: str) -> _BuiltinList[TodoItem]:
        """Return copies of items whose text contains ``query``, ordered by id.

        Matching is a case-insensitive substring match: both the query and the
        item text are NFKC-normalised and casefolded before comparing, so
        composed and decomposed accents match ('e\\u0301' matches 'é') and
        'STRASSE' matches 'Straße'. The query is stripped of surrounding
        whitespace; internal whitespace is significant, so 'buy  milk' does not
        match 'buy milk'. Empty, whitespace-only or non-str queries raise
        ValidationError. No match returns [].
        """
        needle = _fold(_validate_query(query))
        return [
            dataclasses.replace(self._items[i])
            for i in sorted(self._items)
            if needle in _fold(self._items[i].text)
        ]

import os
import sys

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..")))

from todo import TodoItem, TodoList, ValidationError  # noqa: E402


class _OpenStr(str):
    """A str subclass whose value equals 'open'."""


def _populated():
    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a")        # 1 open
    todo.add("b")        # 2 complete
    todo.add("c")        # 3 open
    todo.add("d")        # 4 complete
    todo.complete(2)
    todo.complete(4)
    return todo


def test_open_returns_only_incomplete_items_ordered_by_id():
    result = _populated().filter_by_status("open")
    assert all(isinstance(i, TodoItem) for i in result)
    assert [i.id for i in result] == [1, 3]
    assert all(i.complete is False for i in result)


def test_complete_returns_only_completed_items_ordered_by_id():
    result = _populated().filter_by_status("complete")
    assert [i.id for i in result] == [2, 4]
    assert all(i.complete is True for i in result)


def test_empty_list_filters_return_empty():
    todo = TodoList()
    assert todo.filter_by_status("open") == []
    assert todo.filter_by_status("complete") == []


def test_no_matches_returns_empty_list():
    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a")
    assert todo.filter_by_status("complete") == []


def test_ordering_holds_after_completing_out_of_order():
    todo = TodoList()
    for t in "abcd":
        todo.add(t)
    todo.complete(4)
    todo.complete(1)
    assert [i.id for i in todo.filter_by_status("complete")] == [1, 4]
    assert [i.id for i in todo.filter_by_status("open")] == [2, 3]


def test_filter_after_delete_skips_gaps_and_stays_ordered():
    todo = TodoList()
    for t in "abcd":
        todo.add(t)      # ids 1..4
    todo.delete(1)
    todo.delete(3)
    todo.complete(4)
    assert [i.id for i in todo.filter_by_status("open")] == [2]
    assert [i.id for i in todo.filter_by_status("complete")] == [4]
    todo.add("e")        # id 5, never reuses 1 or 3
    assert [i.id for i in todo.filter_by_status("open")] == [2, 5]


def test_filter_returns_copies():
    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a")
    result = todo.filter_by_status("open")
    result[0].text = "changed"
    result.clear()
    assert todo.list()[0].text == "a"
    assert len(todo.filter_by_status("open")) == 1


def test_later_complete_does_not_change_earlier_filter_result():
    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a")
    earlier = todo.filter_by_status("open")
    todo.complete(1)
    assert earlier[0].complete is False
    assert todo.filter_by_status("open") == []


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "bad",
    ["", "OPEN", "Complete", "done", " open", None, 1, True, ["open"], _OpenStr("open")],
)
def test_invalid_status_raises_validation_error(bad):
    todo = TodoList()
    todo.add("a")
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        todo.filter_by_status(bad)

"""Tiny in-memory to-do library."""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import datetime
import re
import unicodedata
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional

# Module-level alias so annotations/helpers inside TodoList can still refer to
# the builtin ``list`` even though TodoList defines a method named ``list``.
_BuiltinList = list

PRIORITIES = ("high", "medium", "low")
STATUSES = ("open", "complete")

_ISO_DATE_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}")


class TodoError(Exception):
    """Base class for all to-do errors."""


class ValidationError(TodoError, ValueError):
    """Raised when input values are invalid."""


class ItemNotFoundError(TodoError, KeyError):
    """Raised when an item id does not exist."""

    def __str__(self) -> str:  # KeyError would otherwise repr-quote the message
        return Exception.__str__(self)


@dataclass
class TodoItem:
    id: int
    text: str
    complete: bool = False
    due_date: Optional[datetime.date] = None
    priority: str = "medium"


def _validate_text(text: object) -> str:
    """Return ``text`` stripped of leading/trailing whitespace, or raise.

    Only leading/trailing whitespace is removed; internal whitespace and
    newlines are kept as given.
    """
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        raise ValidationError(f"text must be a str, got {type(text).__name__}")
    stripped = text.strip()
    if not stripped:
        raise ValidationError("text must not be empty or whitespace-only")
    return stripped


def _validate_due_date(due: object) -> Optional[datetime.date]:
    """Normalise a due date: None, a datetime.date, or a strict 'YYYY-MM-DD' str.

    datetime.datetime values are rejected. Strings must match YYYY-MM-DD exactly
    (no surrounding whitespace, no basic/week formats). Anything else raises
    ValidationError.
    """
    if due is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(due, datetime.datetime):
        raise ValidationError("due_date must be a datetime.date, not datetime.datetime")
    if isinstance(due, datetime.date):
        return due
    if isinstance(due, str):
        if not _ISO_DATE_RE.fullmatch(due):
            raise ValidationError(f"due_date string must be YYYY-MM-DD, got {due!r}")
        try:
            return datetime.date.fromisoformat(due)
        except ValueError:
            raise ValidationError(f"due_date string must be a valid date, got {due!r}") from None
    raise ValidationError(
        f"due_date must be a date, an ISO date string or None, got {type(due).__name__}"
    )


def _validate_priority(priority: object) -> str:
    """Return ``priority`` as a plain str if it is one of PRIORITIES, otherwise raise.

    Only exact ``str`` instances are accepted, so str subclasses are rejected
    and never stored.
    """
    if type(priority) is not str or priority not in PRIORITIES:
        raise ValidationError(f"priority must be one of {PRIORITIES}, got {priority!r}")
    return priority


def _validate_status(status: object) -> str:
    """Return ``status`` if it is exactly 'open' or 'complete', otherwise raise.

    Only exact ``str`` instances are accepted; str subclasses are rejected.
    """
    if type(status) is not str or status not in STATUSES:
        raise ValidationError(f"status must be one of {STATUSES}, got {status!r}")
    return status


def _validate_query(query: object) -> str:
    """Return ``query`` stripped of surrounding whitespace, or raise.

    Surrounding whitespace is any Unicode whitespace that ``str.strip`` removes
    (including U+00A0 and U+3000). Internal whitespace is kept as given, so
    'buy  milk' (two spaces) does not match 'buy milk'.
    """
    if not isinstance(query, str):
        raise ValidationError(f"query must be a str, got {type(query).__name__}")
    stripped = query.strip()
    if not stripped:
        raise ValidationError("query must not be empty or whitespace-only")
    return stripped


def _fold(s: str) -> str:
    """Normalise text for case-insensitive matching: NFKC then casefold."""
    return unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", s).casefold()


class TodoList:
    """In-memory collection of TodoItem objects.

    Precedence for all item-targeting methods: the id is validated and looked
    up first (ValidationError for a bad id type/value, ItemNotFoundError for an
    unknown id), then the new value is validated. Values are validated before
    the stored item is touched, so a failed call never changes state.

    Returned items are shallow copies: mutating them does not change the store.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._items: dict[int, TodoItem] = {}
        self._next_id: int = 1

    # ----- helpers -------------------------------------------------------
    def _get_item(self, item_id: object) -> TodoItem:
        """Return the stored item with ``item_id``.

        Raises ValidationError if the id is not a positive int, and
        ItemNotFoundError if no such item exists.
        """
        if isinstance(item_id, bool) or not isinstance(item_id, int):
            raise ValidationError(f"item id must be an int, got {type(item_id).__name__}")
        if item_id < 1:
            raise ValidationError(f"item id must be positive, got {item_id}")
        try:
            return self._items[item_id]
        except KeyError:
            raise ItemNotFoundError(f"no item with id {item_id}") from None

    # ----- public API ----------------------------------------------------
    def add(
        self,
        text: str,
        due_date: Optional[datetime.date] = None,
        priority: str = "medium",
    ) -> TodoItem:
        """Add a new item and return a copy of it.

        Only leading and trailing whitespace is stripped from ``text``;
        internal whitespace (including newlines) is preserved. ``due_date``
        must be a ``datetime.date`` or None (ISO strings are not accepted by
        add(); use set_due_date() for those).
        """
        stripped = _validate_text(text)
        if due_date is not None and not isinstance(due_date, datetime.date):
            raise ValidationError("due_date must be a datetime.date or None")
        due = _validate_due_date(due_date)
        checked_priority = _validate_priority(priority)

        item = TodoItem(
            id=self._next_id,
            text=stripped,
            complete=False,
            due_date=due,
            priority=checked_priority,
        )
        self._items[item.id] = item
        self._next_id += 1
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def list(self) -> _BuiltinList[TodoItem]:
        """Return copies of all items, ordered by id."""
        return [dataclasses.replace(self._items[i]) for i in sorted(self._items)]

    def complete(self, item_id: int) -> TodoItem:
        """Mark the item with ``item_id`` as complete and return a copy of it.

        Completing an already-complete item is allowed and is a no-op.
        Raises ValidationError for a non-int/bool id and ItemNotFoundError
        for an unknown id.
        """
        item = self._get_item(item_id)
        item.complete = True
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def delete(self, item_id: int) -> TodoItem:
        """Remove the item with ``item_id`` and return a copy of it.

        Ids are never reused: later add() calls continue from the highest
        id ever issued. Raises ValidationError for a non-int/bool id and
        ItemNotFoundError if the id is unknown (including already deleted).
        """
        item = self._get_item(item_id)
        del self._items[item.id]
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def rename(self, item_id: int, new_text: str) -> TodoItem:
        """Replace the text of an item and return a copy of it.

        ``new_text`` is stripped like add(). The id is checked before the text.
        On ValidationError the stored text is left unchanged. Raises
        ItemNotFoundError for an unknown id.
        """
        item = self._get_item(item_id)
        checked_text = _validate_text(new_text)
        item.text = checked_text
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def set_due_date(self, item_id: int, due: object) -> TodoItem:
        """Set (or clear, with None) the due date of an item and return a copy.

        Accepts a datetime.date, a strict 'YYYY-MM-DD' string, or None. The id
        is checked before the date. datetime.datetime, malformed or padded
        strings and other types raise ValidationError and leave the stored
        date unchanged.
        """
        item = self._get_item(item_id)
        checked_due = _validate_due_date(due)
        item.due_date = checked_due
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def set_priority(self, item_id: int, priority: str) -> TodoItem:
        """Set the priority of an item ('high', 'medium' or 'low') and return a copy.

        The id is checked before the priority. Any other value (including
        wrong case, None, or str subclasses) raises ValidationError and leaves
        the stored priority unchanged.
        """
        item = self._get_item(item_id)
        checked_priority = _validate_priority(priority)
        item.priority = checked_priority
        return dataclasses.replace(item)

    def filter_by_status(self, status: str) -> _BuiltinList[TodoItem]:
        """Return copies of items matching ``status``, ordered by id.

        ``status`` must be exactly 'open' (incomplete items) or 'complete'
        (completed items). Anything else, including str subclasses, raises
        ValidationError.
        """
        checked = _validate_status(status)
        want_complete = checked == "complete"
        return [
            dataclasses.replace(self._items[i])
            for i in sorted(self._items)
            if self._items[i].complete is want_complete
        ]

    def search(self, query: str) -> _BuiltinList[TodoItem]:
        """Return copies of items whose text contains ``query``, ordered by id.

        Matching is a case-insensitive substring match: both the query and the
        item text are NFKC-normalised and casefolded before comparing, so
        composed and decomposed accents match ('e\\u0301' matches 'é') and
        'STRASSE' matches 'Straße'. The query is stripped of surrounding
        whitespace; internal whitespace is significant, so 'buy  milk' does not
        match 'buy milk'. Empty, whitespace-only or non-str queries raise
        ValidationError. No match returns [].
        """
        needle = _fold(_validate_query(query))
        return [
            dataclasses.replace(self._items[i])
            for i in sorted(self._items)
            if needle in _fold(self._items[i].text)
        ]

def _record(**overrides):
    rec = {
        "id": 1,
        "text": "buy milk",
        "complete": False,
        "due_date": None,
        "priority": "medium",
    }
    rec.update(overrides)
    return rec


def _dump(*records):
    return json.dumps(list(records))

        _record(id=7, text="b"),

    items = todo.list()
